nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light powers the algae, eelgrass and marsh grass that start the estuary food web.

nodes.name: Tides and salt water
nodes.desc: Tides reach about 58 miles up the river, mixing fresh and salt water and flooding the marsh twice a day.

nodes.name: River flow
nodes.desc: Spring floods bring fresh water, silt and nutrients down to the estuary and Long Island Sound.

nodes.name: Marsh mud and nutrients
nodes.desc: Muddy marsh soil holds the nutrients that cordgrass takes up.

nodes.name: Smooth cordgrass
nodes.desc: The low-marsh grass of the tidal flats. It traps sediment at the marsh edge and builds up the land.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting algae that feed filter feeders and small plankton grazers throughout the estuary.

nodes.name: Eelgrass
nodes.desc: A seagrass of shallow sheltered water in Long Island Sound. When it dies it feeds the decomposers.

nodes.name: Canada goose
nodes.desc: A common grazer of grasses and marsh plants along the river and shore.

nodes.name: Atlantic ribbed mussel
nodes.desc: A filter feeder living in cordgrass beds. Its waste adds nitrogen and its mounds help cordgrass take hold.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny grazers of phytoplankton. Young menhaden and shad feed on them.

nodes.name: Atlantic menhaden
nodes.desc: A filter-feeding schooling fish. Striped bass, ospreys and eagles all prey on it.

nodes.name: American shad
nodes.desc: A plankton-feeding fish that runs up the Connecticut River to spawn. Striped bass are its main predator and harbor seals take some.

nodes.name: Blue crab
nodes.desc: An omnivorous marsh and estuary crab that preys on ribbed mussels.

nodes.name: Raccoon
nodes.desc: Forages along the marsh edge, where it takes ribbed mussels among many other foods.

nodes.name: American herring gull
nodes.desc: A shoreline generalist that eats shellfish and scavenges dead fish.

nodes.name: Striped bass
nodes.desc: Spends its adult life mostly in salt water and enters rivers to spawn. Feeds on shad, river herring and menhaden.

nodes.name: Osprey
nodes.desc: Fish are about 99 percent of its diet. Nests on platforms and poles along the river and marsh.

nodes.name: Bald eagle
nodes.desc: Takes fish such as menhaden along the river and shore, and also eats carrion.

nodes.name: Harbor seal
nodes.desc: Hunts fish in Long Island Sound and has been recorded as far up the river as Holyoke, Massachusetts.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead cordgrass, eelgrass and algae, returning nutrients to the mud.
